added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: the aggregate line states "keep 6 (ranked above), merge 6, close 5" while the seventeen rows carry keep 6, merge 5 and close 6, so the merge and close counts are transposed in the sentence a reader sums across the batches; the same transposition is carried by the reviewed manifest's wait_condition ("the six keeps and six merges are proposals") and follow_ons ("the six merge and five close proposals"), so both surfaces need one correction, while the rows themselves and the figure's legend colours are unaffected.

the caption states "The four fully-present plans are proposed close; no kept plan's bar is full, because each kept plan carries remaining or in-flight work" while the rows carry eight fully-present plans — six close and two kept, the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet at 7/7 and the-fleet-reports-its-velocity at 4/4 — and the figure it captions draws both kept plans' bars full in orange, so the caption's count is wrong by four and its second clause is contradicted by the drawing it sits under.

item_verdicts.diff: commit 6f320ffd, read against base 40d23d9b, adds 319 lines across two new files, the fragment and the figure; the figure's seventeen bars match all seventeen rows in width and disposition colour, re-derived from the SVG (logs-figure-map.txt: counters 7/7 and velocity 4/4 drawn full orange, the fully-present close rows full green, the partial bars at 9/11, 5/6, 3/9, 1/4, 2/7 and 3/5 all matching their fractions), so the drawing is faithful and the caption is the one place it diverges.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when requires each plan's implementable-or-done section count read from the plan declarations at head with a file and symbol showing each counted section present, plus the last coordinator, a disposition and the keep count; I ran the fragment's own embedded command verbatim from the worktree root and it prints all seventeen checked counts matching the table exactly (logs-denominator.txt), and my citation instrument, behind a positive control, checked 43 cited paths and anchors against 032b03fc: every anchor resolves exactly, the two files it could not open are a claimed absence (reckon/crew/prompts/figure-review.md, whose absence is the row's own point) and a regex artifact (docs/ui/shell.js matched inside the shell.jsx:225 cite), and the three unresolved tokens are prose verbs following accurate code anchors (logs-citations.txt), so the done-when's method holds for all seventeen rows.
item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed node's goal was a read-only fourth triage batch — seventeen pending plans read at main HEAD 032b03fc, each row carrying the section-presence fraction with a cited symbol per counted section, the last coordinator with live runs marked, a proposed disposition and a one-line reason, and the batch keep count summed against the lead's limit of 25; docs/evidence/fragments/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-fourth-batch.html carries all seventeen rows — the slug set is exactly the done-when's seventeen — with the embedded denominator command, the keep-budget paragraph naming 6 against the limit, the figure, and the caption, so the triage itself is delivered in full.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; status complete, the reading head 032b03fc named in evidence_inputs, tests stating none because no source changed with the denominator reproduction as the gate, follow_ons carrying the six keep proposals to the coordinator; it names no baseline_suite or after_suite line because it is not a test node, so the added-failure annotation is unmeasured with that reason rather than a measured zero; its wait_condition and follow_ons repeat the fragment's transposed disposition counts, which the first finding below covers in both places.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares docs/evidence/fragments/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-fourth-batch.html and docs/figures/open-work-is-capped/triage-pending-plans-fourth-batch/ as its write paths, and commit 6f320ffd adds exactly one new file inside each — the fragment and deliverable-presence.svg — with no plan edited and nothing else touched, so the commit's footprint is exactly the declared one.

justifications.durability: the fragment pins its reading head, embeds the command that reproduces its denominators, and commits the figure as a re-derivable SVG, but the two wrong claims are prose nothing will fail on, and the transposition also entered the manifest's wait_condition and follow_ons, so the same correction is owed in two surfaces.
justifications.evidence: the evidence layer is strong — 43 of 43 citations resolve exactly at the stated head behind a positive control, all seventeen denominators reproduce by the fragment's own embedded command, and the figure was re-derived from its SVG and matches every row — but two prose claims are contradicted by the record's own data; separately, the last-coordinator column matches the live ledger exactly for 14 of 17 plans, the three that differ being three of the four cells marked LIVE where a newer session now occupies the slot, and since the manifest's evidence names the live ledger rather than a pinned snapshot that difference cannot be ordered against its read time by any instrument this review has, so it is recorded and not scored.
justifications.fit: the fragment uses the evidence-fragment contract (docs-project, reckon-type=evidence and plan-slug metas, the fragments directory named for its plan, the figure under docs/figures/<plan>/<batch>/ as deliverable-presence.svg), its figure reference resolves under project reckon in the doc audit, and the commit carries a conventional subject and a body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the triage is delivered in full and every fraction and citation reproduces, but the record's own aggregate line transposes the merge and close counts, so one clause of the sentence a reader sums against the other batches is wrong.
justifications.scope_discipline: the commit touches exactly the two files inside the manifest's declared write paths, no plan or other path is edited, and the node returned the disposition proposals as outcome data rather than acting on them.
